diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $u$ be the unique entropy solution of \eqref{eq:conservation_law} with initial condition $u_0 \in L^\infty(\Omega) \cap BV(\Omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The residual R_theta(D_k) only evaluates F(U_theta) on a face lying on the domain boundary. It contains no boundary datum (inflow state, wall condition, etc.), so it cannot enforce any prescribed boundary condition. The convergence framework has the same gap. E_R uses test functions compactly supported in the open domain, so it sees no boundary information. The Bouchut-Perthame estimate is quoted for an initial-value problem with no boundary data. Theorem 2 is nevertheless stated on a bounded Omega with 'the entropy solution', which is not well defined without boundary conditions. Bounded domains with unspecified boundary behaviour are used throughout the experiments.

failure_location.quote: the flux integration across this face directly enforces the prescribed boundary conditions naturally through the evaluation of $R_\theta(D_k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add an explicit boundary-data term or weak boundary entropy condition to the loss and the analysis, or restrict the claims and Theorem 2 to periodic/whole-space settings or to times before waves reach the boundary.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that boundary conditions are handled seamlessly is unsupported. The convergence theorem is only meaningful for Cauchy or periodic problems, or for waves that never reach the boundary, and the bounded-domain experiments are not covered.
issues.title: Boundary conditions claimed to be enforced by the flux residual, but no boundary data enter the loss or the theory
issues.why_classification: A contained restriction or added term is needed, and the main method and rate survive for the restricted setting, but the claimed scope on bounded domains is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Applying the triangle inequality and H\"older's inequality, we bound the integral by factoring out the derivatives of $\varphi$:
Since $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}$, its Lipschitz constant is bounded by $1$. The factor containing $\varphi$ is therefore neutralized:

issues.failure_explanation: R_{k,phi} is the integral of a flux-type vector J_k(U) against grad phi, with phi non-constant on each D_i. The divergence theorem gives the integral of phi*(J_k . n) over the faces minus the integral of phi*div J_k, and phi varies along the faces. This is not a boundary flux residual of U_theta. Hölder's inequality gives only ||grad phi||_inf times ||J_k(U)||_{L^1}, which is O(1) and not small. The displayed inequality bounding R_{k,phi} by sum_i(||phi_t||+||grad phi||)(|R_cons(D_i)|+|R_ent(D_i,k)|) therefore has no valid derivation. Relating a dual-norm entropy defect to cell-boundary residuals would need an approximation argument, for example phi frozen per cell with a mesh-size error. None is given, and it cannot be bounded by the stated losses alone.

failure_location.quote: Applying the divergence theorem on each $D_i$, the continuous residual translates into boundary flux integrals, corresponding exactly to the local conservation residual $R_{\mathrm{cons}}(D_i)$ and entropy residual $R_{\mathrm{ent}}(D_i, k)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a new lemma is needed that bounds the Kruzkov-defect dual norm by cell-boundary residuals. It must include a phi-variation or mesh-size error term and explicit assumptions on the partition and on U_theta.
issues.overall_effect: The link between the implemented losses and the weak truncation error E_R, the core of the paper's theory, is unproven. The L1 bound in Theorem 2 and the 'first explicit L1 convergence rate' claim are unsupported.
issues.title: Lemma 1: reduction of the Kruzkov residual with test function phi to cell-boundary flux residuals is unjustified
issues.why_classification: This is the only bridge between the loss and the Bouchut-Perthame error functional. Repairing it needs a new analysis and probably extra assumptions or error terms, not a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: There are three mismatches. (a) R_ent(D_i,k) is never defined. The implemented L_ent uses one fixed entropy pair (eta,q), e.g. u^2/2, whereas E_R takes a sup over all k of the Kruzkov entropies |u-k|, which are not controlled by one entropy. (b) The proof bounds |R_ent|, but L_ent penalizes only max{0,E}. L_ent is zero for volumes with strongly negative E, i.e. strict dissipation, so |E| is not controlled. (c) With the stated sign, R_{k,phi}(u) is >= 0 for an exact entropy solution and phi >= 0. Counterexample: Burgers shock u=1 for x<t/2, 0 otherwise. Take U_theta = u on rectangles, so L_cons = L_ent = 0 (u^2/2 satisfies the entropy inequality). For k=1/2 the Kruzkov dissipation on the shock is 1/4, so E_R(u) > 0, contradicting the lemma's bound E_R <= 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine E_R with the correct sign, i.e. only the positive part of the Kruzkov entropy production. Replace L_ent by a loss over sampled Kruzkov pairs (|u-k|, sgn(u-k)(F(u)-F(k))) with the one-sided penalty, and re-prove the bound for that loss. The implemented single-entropy method then needs modification.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false as stated, and E_R does not vanish at the exact entropy solution. Theorem 2's claim that the L1 error is controlled by the implemented L_ent is unsupported, and the claim that the loss selects the entropy solution has no proof.
issues.title: Lemma 1: entropy defect over all Kruzkov entropies and with sign/absolute value is not controlled by the one-sided single-entropy loss L_ent
issues.why_classification: The implemented entropy loss does not control the quantity that drives the error estimate, and the lemma is false as written. Repair needs a different loss and a redone argument, so the advertised guarantee for the implemented method is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any partition $\{D_i\}_{i=1}^{N_D}$ of $\Omega \times (0,T)$, the continuous weak truncation error is bounded by the volume-weighted network losses:
Sample space--time subdomains $\{D_k\}_{k=1}^{N_D}$ at multiple scales.

issues.failure_explanation: Cauchy-Schwarz gives sum_i |R_i| <= (sum_i |R_i|^2/|D_i|)^{1/2} (sum_i |D_i|)^{1/2}. By definition, sum_i |R_i|^2/|D_i| = N_D * L_cons because L_cons carries the factor 1/N_D. The correct bound therefore carries an extra sqrt(N_D), and the stated N_D-free bound is false. Example: with equal cells and |R_i| = r*sqrt(|D_i|), sum|R_i| = r*sqrt(N_D|Omega_T|) while the claimed bound is r*sqrt(|Omega_T|). The lemma also requires a partition of the whole space-time domain. The method instead uses randomly resampled, overlapping, multi-scale rectangles, so the lemma's losses are not the trained losses.

failure_location.quote: Recognizing that $\sum |D_i| = |\Omega \times (0,T)|$ and substituting the definitions of $L_{\mathrm{cons}}(\theta)$ and $L_{\mathrm{ent}}(\theta)$ defined in Section 3, we obtain the upper bound for any $\varphi \in \mathcal{A}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor sqrt(N_D) (or drop the 1/N_D normalization), make K_opt depend on the fixed partition size, and state precisely which fixed partition the theorem's losses refer to.
issues.overall_effect: The constant in Lemma 1 and in K_opt acquires an N_D^{1/4} factor, which grows under refinement. The theorem is not matched to the sampled-volume loss actually trained.
issues.title: Lemma 1: normalization 1/N_D in the losses dropped, and partition assumed while sampled overlapping volumes are used
issues.why_classification: A local constant correction and a clarification of the setting keep the lemma's form, the exponent and the qualitative convergence statement for fixed N_D.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem allows u_0 in BV with jumps, and every Burgers test has a jump at t=0. The network N_theta is continuous, so U_theta(.,t) keeps a jump of size (1-tau(t))[U_0] at the initial discontinuity location for all t<T. This jump is stationary, while the exact entropy solution moves it (e.g. speed 1/2). Satisfying Rankine-Hugoniot for such a fixed jump would force a spurious stationary shock, or an unbounded N_theta as t->0. So L_cons -> 0 and L_ent -> 0 cannot hold together with convergence to the entropy solution, and the hypotheses are essentially vacuous for discontinuous data. The reported nonzero t=0 errors (L_inf 0.795) also contradict the claimed exact initial condition.

failure_location.quote: By construction of the temporal ansatz, $U_\theta(x,0) = u_0(x)$ for all $x \in \Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the exact-IC claim for discontinuous data, use an initial-condition penalty or weak initial-data term, and keep ||U_theta(.,0)-u_0||_{L1} in the bound (the Bouchut-Perthame statement already has it), or restrict the theorem to continuous u_0.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 2 does not cover the discontinuous-data problems it is applied to. The claim that the initial-condition error is eliminated is unsound for those problems.
issues.title: Exact-initial-condition ansatz forces a stationary discontinuity for discontinuous u_0, so hypotheses 3-4 and Step 1 conflict with the claimed convergence
issues.why_classification: The repair adds an initial-data term to the loss and bound and changes the ansatz, but the overall structure and rate survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The convergence rate of $1/4$ is optimal for arbitrary control volume partitions.

issues.failure_explanation: The first line of Step 4 (the cited estimate) is C*sqrt(TV(u_0)*M)*E_R^{1/4}, since sqrt(TV*M*sqrt(E_R)) = sqrt(TV*M)*E_R^{1/4}. The second line uses sqrt(TV*M)*E_R^{1/2}, silently dropping a square root. Inserting E_R <= |Omega_T|^{1/2}(sqrt(L_c)+sqrt(L_e)) into E_R^{1/4} gives |Omega_T|^{1/8}(L_c^{1/8}+L_e^{1/8}), i.e. rate 1/8 in the losses. The stated K_opt and the exponent 1/4 do not follow from the cited estimate and Lemma 1. The remark's optimality claim for arbitrary partitions, and the improvement to 1/2 on structured grids, are asserted without any argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with exponent 1/8 and K_opt = C*sqrt(TV(u_0)*M)*|Omega_T|^{1/8}, and remove or justify the optimality and structured-grid remarks.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit rate L^{1/4} (and the remark on optimality) is unsupported. What follows is L^{1/8}, given Lemma 1.
issues.title: Step 4 of Theorem 2 loses a square root; the derived rate is 1/8, and the '1/4 is optimal' remark is unsupported
issues.why_classification: Convergence survives but the headline rate exponent is halved; the fix is a contained restatement, not a new architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In all cases, the entropy functions are convex and the corresponding entropy fluxes satisfy the compatibility condition with the physical flux, ensuring consistency with the entropy inequality.

issues.failure_explanation: For the shallow water system with energy eta = h|u|^2/2 + g h^2/2, the compatible energy flux is q = (eta + g h^2/2) u, i.e. u times (energy plus pressure), as for the Euler pair. The stated q = eta*u omits the pressure-work term g h^2 u/2. For smooth solutions d_t eta + div(eta u) = -div(g h^2 u/2), which is nonzero in general. The compatibility relation grad q = grad eta grad F therefore fails, contrary to the claim, and E_theta(D) is nonzero even for smooth exact solutions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the flux by q = (eta + g h^2/2) u (componentwise for the velocity vector u), and re-verify or rerun the shallow-water experiments with this pair.
issues.overall_effect: The entropy loss for shallow water (1D dam break, 2D cases) is built on an invalid entropy pair. It can penalize admissible smooth flow, and the stated consistency with the entropy inequality does not hold.
issues.title: Shallow-water entropy flux q = eta*u is incorrect; compatibility claim fails
issues.why_classification: The formula fix is local, but the shallow-water entropy loss and the experiments that depend on it need to be redone.
